title: Jordan arrests 3 suspects in deadly church attack, state media says
summary: Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects after a shootout on Monday in connection with an attack on a church last week that killed nine people, state television reported.

image.caption: Sahar Al-Halsa, who survived Friday's shooting at the church, gestures toward it while recounting what she witnessed during the attack, as she speaks to Reuters at her home next to the church in Karak, Jordan. (Alaa Al Sukhni/Reuters)

blocks.text: Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects after a shootout on Monday in connection with an attack on a church last week that killed nine people, state television reported.
Suspects were found hiding in abandoned house, authorities say

Jordanian security forces arrested three armed suspects after a shootout on Monday in connection with an attack on a church in the U.S.-allied country that killed nine people, state television reported.

Friday's attack during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud, in Karak governorate, about 120 kilometres southwest of the capital of Amman, also wounded 40 others. Witnesses said the shooting lasted several minutes.

Jordan's Public Security Directorate said the suspects were located while hiding in an abandoned house in Karak. They refused to surrender and attacked security forces, who returned fire and arrested all three after wounding them, the directorate said in a statement published on state media.
No security personnel were injured, it said, and a number of firearms and ammunition were found in the suspects' possession.

items: Jordan king orders 'iron fist' response amid search for suspects in deadly church attack

blocks.text: Jordanian authorities have said the violence was carried out by "extremist terrorists." There has been no claim of responsibility.
A building shows signs of gunfire at the site where Jordanian security forces arrested three suspects in connection with Friday's shooting. (Alaa Al Sukhni/Reuters)
"Terrorism has no place among us," the directorate said, adding that the suspects had met their "just fate."
King Abdullah, a U.S. partner in the fight against Islamist militant groups, has ordered security forces to respond with an "iron fist" to the rare attack on the Christian minority.
Such violence is highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable state in the Middle East, though authorities say they have foiled several Islamist militant plots over the years.
The Public Security Directorate did not name the suspects or publicly identify possible affiliations with any Islamist militant groups.
Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities were reviewing the circumstances that led young people toward extremism and would hold accountable anyone found to have participated in the attack.
